rules.title: A defect in the logic of the change
rules.description: The change makes the code do the wrong thing: a wrong result, a call that always throws, removed validation that lets invalid input through, or code that has become unreachable. Use it for a defect in the logic that no more specific rule names, on the line where the defect is, which may be outside the hunks when a change elsewhere breaks it. Lower the severity when the defect cannot crash or corrupt data.
rules.why: State what goes wrong at runtime, and for which input or path.
rules.fix: State the smallest change that restores the intended behaviour, for example the check to put back or the call to make first.

rules.title: A change in one variant without its counterpart
rules.description: A change under one flavor or product-variant source set has no counterpart in the others, and the feature is not deliberately variant-specific. A file changed under `src/<variant>/` whose counterpart under another variant of the configuration exists and is not changed is a candidate. Not checked in single-variant repositories.
rules.why: The variants now behave differently, and the ones left unchanged ship without the change.
rules.fix: Make the matching change in the other variants, or move the code to a source set they share.

rules.title: Relies on an undeclared change of a shared library
rules.description: The change request relies on a change in a shared library (a new version, a new or changed symbol) and its Related Changes section has no entry for it. The shared libraries are the sharedLibraries of the repository criteria, as project keys.

rules.title: Removes API that a related change still uses
rules.description: The change request removes a public symbol, or makes it hidden, that the repository of a change request above it in the cascade still uses. A removed public declaration is a candidate on its removed line, with a reference to each use found in the repositories of its ancestors, the root included: on their target branch outside the lines they remove or replace, and on the lines they add. Uses are found by name in code: a search match only in a comment or a string of its line is dropped, but one inside a block comment opened on an earlier line is kept. Judge whether each use is really the removed symbol.
rules.why: The consumer still uses the removed symbol, so its build breaks as soon as it takes this change.
rules.fix: Migrate the consumers first, in the related change requests, or keep the symbol, deprecated, for one more release.

rules.title: Adds a required parameter that a related change does not pass
rules.description: The change request gives a public function a parameter without a default, and the repository of a change request above it in the cascade still calls it. A function with a single overload that gains such a parameter is a candidate on its declaration at head, with a reference to each call on the target branch of its ancestors that they do not remove or replace. Calls are found by name in code: a search match only in a comment or a string of its line is dropped, but one inside a block comment opened on an earlier line is kept. Judge whether each call is really this function and whether it passes the argument.
rules.why: The callers do not pass the new argument, so their build breaks as soon as they take this change.
rules.fix: Give the parameter a default value, or update the callers in the related change requests.

rules.title: Uses a changed API against its new contract
rules.description: The change request uses an API changed by a related change request against its new contract: nullability, threading or error behaviour. Reported on this change request's lines.
